$comment: RESEARCH WORKLIST for the payer directory — WHO to cover and WHAT to ask, never the answers.
Answers come only from primary sources fetched during the monthly refresh, cited inline, per the
VERIFIED-ONLY rule in docs/monthly-refresh.md. Nothing here is copied from any third party's material.
Origin: a coverage gap analysis run 2026-09-17 against src/data/payers/*.ts. Commercial coverage at
that point was four carrier families (Aetna, Cigna, UnitedHealthcare, Anthem GA) across 19 states;
these are the payers that actually appear on ABA leads in those same states and had no guide.

ruleFields.label: Age limit
ruleFields.question: What upper (and any lower) age bound does this payer put on the ABA benefit, and does EPSDT change it?
ruleFields.sourceHint: State manual eligibility section; payer clinical policy; state autism mandate statute.

ruleFields.label: Diagnosis recency
ruleFields.question: How recent must the diagnostic evaluation be, and what restarts the clock?
ruleFields.sourceHint: State manual documentation/PA section; payer medical-necessity criteria.

ruleFields.label: Who may diagnose
ruleFields.question: Which credentials may make the ASD diagnosis this payer will accept?
ruleFields.sourceHint: Payer medical-necessity criteria; state manual diagnosing-provider list.

ruleFields.label: Diagnostic tools required
ruleFields.question: Which standardized instruments must sit behind the diagnosis (ADOS-2, ADI-R, Vineland, CARS-2)?
ruleFields.sourceHint: Payer criteria document; state manual assessment section.

ruleFields.label: Referral required?
ruleFields.question: Is a referral or order required, from whom, and how current must it be?
ruleFields.sourceHint: State manual PA/ordering section; payer precert requirements.

ruleFields.label: Telehealth
ruleFields.question: Which ABA codes may be delivered remotely, with which POS codes, and with what in-person floor?
ruleFields.sourceHint: State telehealth policy/manual; payer telehealth reimbursement policy; CMS telehealth list.

ruleFields.label: Supervision
ruleFields.question: What supervision does this payer require over technicians delivering 97153 — percentage floor, ratio cap, direct vs. asynchronous, and who may supervise?
ruleFields.sourceHint: State Medicaid provider/billing manual; payer ABA clinical policy; provider agreement.

ruleFields.label: Concurrent billing (97153 + 97155)
ruleFields.question: May 97153 and 97155 be billed for the same clock time, and under what conditions (direction-of-technician vs. direct treatment)?
ruleFields.sourceHint: Payer reimbursement policy; state manual concurrent-services section; NCCI/CMS edits.

ruleFields.label: Daily limits / MUEs
ruleFields.question: What per-day unit ceilings apply per code, and does the payer follow the Medicaid or the Practitioner MUE table, or publish its own?
ruleFields.sourceHint: CMS MUE tables (two different tables); payer reimbursement policy; state fee schedule.

ruleFields.label: Session-note signature
ruleFields.question: Who must sign each session note, and within what timeframe?
ruleFields.sourceHint: State manual documentation standards; payer audit/documentation policy.

ruleFields.label: Place of service
ruleFields.question: Is ABA payable in school, community and group home, and with which POS codes or restrictions?
ruleFields.sourceHint: State manual place-of-service section; payer policy; POS code table.

ruleFields.label: Bill as provider
ruleFields.question: Whose NPI must the claim carry, and what modifiers ride along?
ruleFields.sourceHint: State manual billing section; payer claims guide; enrollment rules.

ruleFieldBacklog.target: Every guide in src/data/payers/*.ts carries both field groups (12 fields) for as many as primary sources support. Measured by `node scripts/payer-coverage.mjs`; no group may regress.
ruleFieldBacklog.order: State Medicaid guides first (their manuals answer all six in one document and MCOs inherit the floor), then Medicaid MCOs where the plan deviates from the state rule, then commercial.
ruleFieldBacklog.cadence: Fill the six fields for at least two state programs and their MCOs each refresh; omit a field rather than guess.
ruleFieldBacklog.progressNote: deliveryRules pass run 2026-09-17 across GA, NJ and MA. 'verified' = a fetched primary source states the rule; 'plan-dependent' = the rule genuinely varies by plan or the published sources conflict; 'unverified' = the field carries a note plus a verifyVia naming the portal, phone line or document that would settle it; 'omitted' = no source and no useful verifyVia. Blocked or unreachable sources this pass: GAMMIS (mmis.georgia.gov) refuses connections, so Georgia's current quarterly ASD manual and live fee schedule could not be read — the posted January 2018 Part II manual is what Georgia's entries rest on and it predates the 97151-97158 code set. mass.gov returns 403 to automated fetches, so the MassHealth ABA Provider FAQ was not read. The NJ DMAHS ABA newsletter was retrievable only by direct download from web.archive.org. horizonnjhealth.com and aetnabetterhealth.com return HTML stubs or 403 to automated fetches, so no Horizon NJ Health or Aetna Better Health of NJ ABA document could be read.
ruleFieldBacklog.method: Extraction before research: where a guide's own cited prose already states the fact, lift it into the field with the same citation. Only research what prose does not cover.

verifyClaims.claim: The guide presents CG-BEH-02 (Adaptive Behavioral Treatment) as Anthem's live ABA medical-necessity criteria.
verifyClaims.challenge: Research on 2026-09-17 found Anthem commercial transitioned ABA reviews from CG-BEH-02 and MCG W0153 to MCG B-806-T for dates of service on or after 2024-06-01, evidenced by a signed Anthem regional-officer letter (Colorado version) and doc code MULTI-BCBS-CM-047274-23 in five other states. NOT independently re-verified — anthem.com and providernews.anthem.com are JS-rendered and were unreachable at verification time.
verifyClaims.resolve: Fetch the transition notice via browser or text proxy and Anthem's guideline index; if confirmed, correct anthem-bcbs-georgia and any vob/ layer referencing CG-BEH-02 for ABA.

verifyClaims.claim: Cites the October 2024 multi-state ABA Provider Resource Guide.
verifyClaims.challenge: A June 2025 edition (MULTI-BCBS-CM-084583-25-CPN83931) appears to supersede it, covering CT/GA/IN/KY/ME/MO/NV/NH/NY/OH/VA. Colorado is excluded and has its own state guide (COBCBS-CM-084607-25).
verifyClaims.resolve: Confirm the June 2025 edition and reprint the citation.

verifyClaims.claim: States Georgia reimburses 97151-97158 in 15-minute units with U1-U5 practitioner modifiers.
verifyClaims.challenge: The publicly posted Part II ASD manual (Jan 2018) contains ZERO occurrences of 97151-97158 and 147 of the retired Category III set (0359T-0374T), priced in 90- and 30-minute units. The modern code set is almost certainly what Georgia actually pays, but the claim is currently unsourced because the live fee schedule sits inside GAMMIS. Two further claims ('8 hours per 6-month period' assessment cap; 'telehealth within 50 miles of the border') also appear nowhere in the posted manual.
verifyClaims.resolve: Blocked on DR-001. Do not 'correct' the guide to the legacy codes — the posted manual is the stale artifact, not the guide.
verifyClaims.update_2026_09_17: PARTIAL UNBLOCK found. The GA DCH Part II Telehealth Guidance (version date 10/1/2025) publishes a CURRENT Category I ABS code table — 97151-97158, 0362T, 0373T in 15-minute units with GT plus U1-U5 practitioner modifiers and rates — from a live DCH document, without needing GAMMIS. That corroborates the guide's modern code set and contradicts the posted Jan-2018 ASD manual. Re-verify and re-cite georgia-medicaid's code-set claim against the Telehealth Guidance; the assessment-hours and 50-mile claims remain unresolved.

verifyClaims.claim: 'Telehealth is billable only if the rendering provider is in Georgia or within 50 miles of the border', cited to the Part II ASD Policy Manual.
verifyClaims.challenge: That manual has NO telehealth section — neither 'telehealth' nor 'telemedicine' appears in it. The current DCH Part II Telehealth Guidance (10/1/2025) does not carry the rule either: its distant-site definition turns on Georgia practice authority (O.C.G.A. 43-34-31), and its only 50-mile reference is about ambulance transportation. CareSource MM-0212 does assert the rule and attributes it to that guidance.
verifyClaims.resolve: Either find the version CareSource is restating, or drop the claim. The citation is wrong either way.

verifyClaims.claim: 'Standardized developmental assessments at minimum every 2 years' and 'protocol modification up to 2 hours per 10 direct hours, max 8/week', both cited to the Anthem ABA Provider Resource Guide (Oct 2024).
verifyClaims.challenge: That PDF was read in full and contains NEITHER statement. It says only that documentation must show the treatment plan was reviewed and/or updated at least every six months, and defers unit limits to CMS MUEs. Both facts likely come from CG-BEH-02, which is not public at the cited URL.
verifyClaims.resolve: Re-source both or remove them. Pairs with VC-001 (the CG-BEH-02 retirement question).
verifyClaims.evidence_2026_09_17: CONFIRMED and widened. The cited PDF was downloaded (HTTP 200, 388KB, real PDF) and pdftotext'd in full: ZERO occurrences of 'prior authorization', 'precertification' or 'preauthoriz'; ZERO of '20 hours'; ZERO of 'CG-BEH', 'MCG' or any ASD-diagnosis criterion. So anthem-bcbs-georgia's assessmentPA, treatmentPA and dxRequired are ALSO unsourced by it, not just the two facts originally flagged. All three are now status 'unverified' with blocker 'document'. SEPARATE LEAD: the PDF's cover lists 11 states (CT GA IN KY ME MO NV NH NY OH VA), which is the June 2025 edition's state list per VC-002 — the old doc-code URL may already be serving the newer edition.

verifyClaims.claim: Non-participating claims 'default-pay at a percentage of the Florida Medicaid allowable fee schedule'; pre-existing Acentra authorizations auto-extended 120 days.
verifyClaims.challenge: The current flyer (1025703FL0626) says non-par pay is the LESSER of the amount specified in the authorization request form or 100% of the applicable Medicaid fee schedule — 100%, and a lesser-of test — and that continuity runs up to 90 days, not 120. The guide cites the older 675204FL0225 edition, so it may have been right at carve-in.
verifyClaims.resolve: Re-verify against the current flyer edition and update both figures.

verifyClaims.claim: Cites CareSource MM-0212 effective 1/1/2025 throughout.
verifyClaims.challenge: A newer edition effective 7/1/2026 is published at .../medicaid-ga-policy-medical-mm-0212-20260701.
verifyClaims.resolve: Re-verify against the 7/1/2026 edition and reprint citations.

verifyClaims.claim: deliveryRules is incomplete — placeOfService and billAsProvider are absent.
verifyClaims.challenge: Left untouched during the Georgia backfill because that file's delivery rules were out of scope for the agent that filled its intake gates.
verifyClaims.resolve: Fill both fields next cycle.

verifyClaims.claim: RESOLVED 2026-09-17 — recorded for audit trail.
verifyClaims.challenge: dxRequired read 'Yes — ASD diagnosis by a qualified professional (DMAS)' on six guides. DMAS Appendix D (rev. 7/17/2025) contains ZERO occurrences of 'autism'; admission turns on a youth under 21 with a primary ICD/DSM diagnosis in the disruptive-behaviour, mood, substance-use or trauma-and-stressor categories, or a provisional psychiatric diagnosis from an LMHP when none is definitive, plus two functional-impairment criteria. Also corrected: prose claiming DMAS sets no supervision frequency — Appendix D requires monthly observation of the youth and twice-monthly supervision of unlicensed staff.
verifyClaims.resolve: DONE. Verified against the primary document and applied.
verifyClaims.correction_of_the_correction: 2026-09-17, same day. The fix I applied was itself partly wrong, by the exact mechanism it was fixing. My extraction regex matched the FIRST occurrence of 'primary ICD diagnosis' in Appendix D — which belongs to FFT (p.14), not ABA (p.24) — so I imported FFT's diagnostic-category list ('disruptive behavior, mood, substance use or trauma and stressor-related') into the ABA criterion, which has no category list at all. The ABA criterion is BROADER than my corrected value claimed. Caught by a later agent, re-verified by counting occurrences and locating each one's parent section, and corrected on all six guides. LESSON: when extracting from a multi-service document, never take the first regex hit — count the occurrences and identify which section each belongs to. The supervision correction from the same pass was re-checked the same way and is sound (both quotes are unique and sit in the ABA section).

verifyClaims.slug: north-carolina-medicaid + Healthy Blue, AmeriHealth, Trillium, WellCare NC
verifyClaims.claim: 'Treatment plans are reviewed at least every 6 months and rewritten annually.'
verifyClaims.challenge: The 8/1/2026 CCP 8F revision retitled subsection 5.3.4 and REMOVED 'Annual Rewriting'. Review now triggers on each goal's target date, a change in needs, a change in provider, or a new service, with short-range goals never exceeding 12 months.
verifyClaims.resolve: Re-read CCP 8F 5.3.4 and update the four MCO guides plus the state guide.

verifyClaims.claim: dxRequired names 'ADI-R, ADOS-2, CARS-2, or TELE-ASD-PEDS' as accepted instruments.
verifyClaims.challenge: That list comes from Alliance's Feb 2026 guidance, which predates the rewrite. Finalized CCP 8F 3.2.4 names BOSA, Tele-ASD-Peds, ADOS-2 and CARS2-ST/CARS2-HF — ADI-R is NOT on the state list.
verifyClaims.resolve: Confirm whether Alliance still accepts ADI-R above the state floor, or align to 8F.

verifyClaims.claim: 'At least 10% of approved services should be directly observed by the LQASP.'
verifyClaims.challenge: CCP 8F 6.3(a) says 10% of services PROVIDED BY A PARAPROFESSIONAL — a materially different (and smaller) denominator.
verifyClaims.resolve: Correct the denominator.

verifyClaims.claim: 'Both Sunflower and Optum/UHC require diagnosis validation within the last 6 months', and KMAP 26140 'layers on top of rather than replacing' that rule.
verifyClaims.challenge: Bulletin 26140 states the opposite: once diagnosed by a qualified diagnostician, members are eligible 'without the need for a re-evaluation of their autism spectrum disorder diagnosis. There is also no time limit on how soon they begin autism treatment.' Optum's July-2026 State Mandates supplement reproduces that verbatim for Kansas and no longer carries any 6-month language. Only Sunflower's KS.CP.01 still has it — last reviewed 06/2019, and it concedes state Medicaid provisions take precedence on conflict.
verifyClaims.resolve: Human decision needed on the prose. The dxRecency fields already state both rules and the conflict. NOTE: the 26140 effective date was corrected 2026-09-17 from 9/1/2026 to 11/1/2026 (bulletin reissued 8/31/2026) — verified against the live page.

verifyClaims.claim: Cigna guides credit 'no PA on 97151/97152/0362T' to EN0499; Aetna guides credit precertification to CPB 0554.
verifyClaims.challenge: Both documents were read in full and neither addresses prior authorization at all. The facts are right, the attributions are wrong — they come from the Evernorth autism resource guide and the Aetna BH precertification list (eff. 8/1/2024) respectively.
verifyClaims.resolve: Re-point the citations. Correct URLs are already in cites/sources on the NM/NC/OH guides.
verifyClaims.evidence_2026_09_17: CONFIRMED by direct read. Aetna CPB 0554 was fetched in full: no occurrence of 'precertification' or 'authorization' anywhere, and it is the EXCLUSION bulletin — its code table reads 'CPT codes NOT covered for indications listed in the CPB: 97151 - 97158' and it points to CPB 0648 for ABA-for-autism. The correct source is Aetna's Participating provider behavioral health precertification list (eff. 8/1/2024), which lists ABA 97151-97158, 0362T, 0373T. That citation is now attached to all Aetna guides. REMAINING WORK: the value TEXT still reads "per Aetna's national CPB 0554 policy" in 19 places (one per state file) and now contradicts its own citation. Fix the wording, not the fact.

verifyClaims.claim: Cites 'Optum ABA State Mandates BH803ABASTM12026, effective January 2026' and 'BH803ABASCC'.
verifyClaims.challenge: Live documents at the same URLs are BH803ABASTM72026 (effective July 2026) and BH803ABASCC082025 (interim review April 2026). Substance unchanged for AZ and CO.
verifyClaims.resolve: Refresh the document identifiers and dates.

verifyClaims.claim: dxRequired reads 'ASD only (F84.0-F84.9)'.
verifyClaims.challenge: Aetna's own ABA Medical Necessity Guide prints 'ICD-10/ F84.0; F84.3 - F84.9' — F84.1 and F84.2 are not in its list.
verifyClaims.resolve: Decide whether to narrow the range to Aetna's printed set across the Aetna guides.
verifyClaims.evidence_2026_09_17: NOT a simple error — two Aetna documents disagree. CPB 0554's covered-code table reads 'F84.0 - F84.9 Pervasive developmental disorders', which SUPPORTS the current value. The ABA Medical Necessity Guide ((c)2026) prints 'ICD-10/ F84.0; F84.3 - F84.9', excluding F84.1 and F84.2. Decide which governs, then make dxRequired and diagnosingProviders agree — right now they contradict each other inside the same guides.
verifyClaims.refined_2026_09_17: Scope clarified by a second independent read. F84.1 and F84.4 are not valid ICD-10-CM codes at all, so the practical delta between Aetna's two documents is ONLY F84.2, Rett syndrome. Note Cigna EN0499 makes the same carve-out explicitly: 'F84.0 - F84.9, with the exception of F84.2, Rett syndrome'. The question to settle is therefore narrow and concrete: does Aetna cover ABA for Rett syndrome? CPB 0554's code table says yes; the ABA Medical Necessity Guide that BH reviewers actually apply says no. Four Aetna guides hold unverified pending a ruling.

verifyClaims.claim: RESOLVED 2026-09-17 — recorded for audit trail.
verifyClaims.challenge: atGlance, treatmentPA, cardDesc, metaDescription and body prose all stated a blanket 'up to 180 days' authorization period. CCP 8F 5.1 is TIERED: up to 180 calendar days at 16 hrs/week or fewer, but only up to 90 calendar days above 16 hrs/week. Verified verbatim against the current 8/1/2026 policy PDF. Corrected on north-carolina-medicaid and healthy-blue-north-carolina.
verifyClaims.resolve: DONE.

verifyClaims.claim: The FAQ says 'The state's documents conflict: the MSD caps direct service at 6 hrs/day and 20 hrs/week, while DHHS summaries describe up to 30 hours/week.'
verifyClaims.challenge: The page's own body section says the conflict was resolved in the MSD's favour, and the current live MSD reads 20 cleanly with no 30-hour alternate. The June 2025 archived MSD did read '20-30', which is where the ambiguity came from — but it is gone. The FAQ now contradicts the body of its own page.
verifyClaims.resolve: Reword the FAQ to match the body.

verifyClaims.claim: Prose says the standard PA form is 'completed by the LABA rendering or supervising services.'
verifyClaims.challenge: The form says 'The Board-Certified Behavioral Analyst (BCBA) rendering and/or supervising the services SHOULD complete this form' — 'should', not 'must', and BCBA, not LABA. The LABA requirement comes from the Carelon/MBHP performance spec (262 CMR 10.00), not the form.
verifyClaims.resolve: Attribute each half to the right document.

verifyClaims.claim: dxRequired asserts 'ASD validated within the last 6 months by a licensed psychologist or MD'.
verifyClaims.challenge: The SAME guide's dxRecency field, already status 'verified', records that Optum's current State Mandates supplement (BH803ABASTM72026, July 2026) reproduces KMAP Bulletin 26140 verbatim and no longer contains any 6-month validation language. This is not the Sunflower-vs-state conflict — it is a live funnel value contradicted by the carrier's own current document, inside one guide. Also present in that guide's atGlance row and collect item, and in the kansas-medicaid FAQ answer 'Both Sunflower and Optum/UHC require...'.
verifyClaims.resolve: Highest-priority Kansas fix. Re-read BH803ABASTM72026 and correct the value, atGlance, collect and the FAQ together.

verifyClaims.claim: A $45,000 per calendar year ABA benefit maximum, status 'verified', cited to the plan's Medicaid/CHPlus provider manual.
verifyClaims.challenge: That is a hard dollar cap on an EPSDT benefit for under-21 Medicaid members, which is unusual on its face — and $45,000 is exactly the figure New York's COMMERCIAL mandate carried in 2011 before the (since-repealed) 680-hour cap replaced it. Possible contamination from the commercial mandate history. The manual was not re-fetched.
verifyClaims.resolve: Fetch the Highmark manual and confirm the cap is real, current and applies to the Medicaid line.

verifyClaims.claim: Not a contradiction — a gap.
verifyClaims.challenge: The UHC TN Level of Care Guidelines carry an in-state service-location rule, 'ABA services must be located in TN', which no structured field captures.
verifyClaims.resolve: Add it to placeOfService next cycle.

verifyClaims.claim: deliveryRules.supervision says 'Evernorth publishes no percentage floor or caseload cap for technician supervision.'
verifyClaims.challenge: EN0499 — the document that value's own verifyVia names — does publish one, at 'Supervision / Direction of Treatment' (p.5): direct and indirect case supervision 'is consistent with the general accepted standard of care of one to two hours per ten hours of direct treatment', and 'When direct treatment is 10 hours per week or less, a minimum of one to two hours per week of direct case supervision is provided.'
verifyClaims.resolve: Closeable today — the document is readable. Rewrite the value from EN0499 p.5.
verifyClaims.resolution: DONE. EN0499 fetched and pdftotext'd; the ratio appears exactly once (no first-match ambiguity) at 'Supervision / Direction of Treatment': direct plus indirect case supervision 'is consistent with the general accepted standard of care of one to two hours per ten hours of direct treatment', and 'when direct treatment is 10 hours per week or less, a minimum of one to two hours per week of direct case supervision is provided.' Corrected on all 5 guides that carried the denial (FL, GA, MA, NE, NJ) and set to verified with the EN0499 citation.

verifyClaims.claim: Submit authorizations by fax 888-977-0776 (in treatmentPA, atGlance, prose and an FAQ).
verifyClaims.challenge: The guide's own cited Point32Health source lists 888-977-0776 under Tufts Health DIRECT, and publishes no fax number for Tufts Health Together. A Together packet sent there plausibly bounces.
verifyClaims.resolve: Find Together's actual submission route and correct all four places.

verifyClaims.claim: Not an error in our data — a live conflict worth surfacing to partners.
verifyClaims.challenge: Aetna CPB 0554 states ABA is 'experimental, investigational, or unproven for Down Syndrome in the absence of an autism spectrum disorder co-morbidity' and lists Q90.0-Q90.9 as not covered — against Massachusetts Ch. 388's Down-syndrome mandate effective 1/1/2026. Aetna has published no MA deviation, unlike Optum. A fully-insured MA family could be denied on a policy Aetna has not updated.
verifyClaims.resolve: Keep dxRequired plan-dependent; consider saying this explicitly in the guide prose so intake can escalate on parity/mandate grounds.

verifyClaims.claim: Eleven fields open with 'ABA is carved out of every Utah Medicaid ACO to state fee-for-service.'
verifyClaims.challenge: The January 2026 Utah ASD manual carves out ASD-related MEDICAL services (PT/OT/ST) and the diagnostic evaluation to FFS — not ABA therapy itself. Not a refutation, but the manual does not carry the claim.
verifyClaims.resolve: Source the ABA carve-out specifically or soften the eleven values.

verifyClaims.slug: unitedhealthcare-* commercial (NC, NM, OH, and others)
verifyClaims.claim: 'Reviews every 4-6 months' reauthorization cadence, and a 'two-step assessment-then-treatment' structure.
verifyClaims.challenge: Optum ABA Supplemental Clinical Criteria (BH803ABASCC) was read in full by two independent agents. It states 'Prior authorization is required for ABA' and mentions 'within a 6-month period' only for inadequate progress. Neither the 4-6 month cadence nor the two-step structure appears anywhere in it.
verifyClaims.resolve: Re-source or drop both claims wherever they appear.

verifyClaims.claim: FAQ cites PB 25-02 as a live source describing 'up to 30 hours/week'.
verifyClaims.challenge: PB 25-02 does say 30 hours — but it was SUPERSEDED by PB 26-06 (eff. 7/1/2026), which sets 20 hrs/week cleanly. The guide body and the verified dailyLimits field are right; the FAQ quotes a superseded bulletin as if current.
verifyClaims.resolve: Update the FAQ to name only the DHHS 'ABA Facts' page as the stale source. Supersedes VC-018.

verifyClaims.claim: dxRecency value opens 'No recency window could be sourced'.
verifyClaims.challenge: It is now sourced — the January 2026 manual (reached via r.jina.ai) confirms no recency window exists, and the field is status 'verified'. The wording is a leftover from when it was unreachable.
verifyClaims.resolve: Wording pass: say the manual sets no recency window, not that we could not find one.

verifyClaims.slug: all commercial guides with a flat 'Yes' on PA (consistency review)
verifyClaims.claim: assessmentPA/treatmentPA read 'Yes — required' flatly on commercial carriers.
verifyClaims.challenge: Anthem's Central Blues precertification list says it applies to fully-insured members and to self-insured (ASO) members ONLY where the group purchased the medical-management program — otherwise 'preapproval is not required and clinical review will not be performed'. The National Accounts list says ABA precert 'applies unless the group specifically opts out'. Anthem BCBS Indiana and Missouri were set to plan-dependent on that basis; Aetna, Cigna and Optum were left verified because their documents state the requirement without a published opt-out.
verifyClaims.resolve: Decide whether the self-funded opt-out caveat should be applied consistently across all commercial PA fields, or whether the Anthem-specific published opt-out genuinely distinguishes it. A judgement call, not a fetch.

verifyClaims.claim: assessmentPA says 'form GR-69017-4, eff. 1/1/2026'.
verifyClaims.challenge: The form Aetna currently publishes is stamped GR-69017-4 (7-26) — a July 2026 revision. The form number matches; the date label looks stale.
verifyClaims.resolve: Confirm the current revision date and update the label.

verifyClaims.slug: indiana MCO guides: anthem-indiana-medicaid, mhs-indiana, caresource-indiana, mdwise-indiana, unitedhealthcare-community-plan-indiana
verifyClaims.claim: Each ABA PA is capped at 6 months (treatmentPA / atGlance / deliveryRules prose / FAQ).
verifyClaims.challenge: IC 27-1-37.5-26(b) (eff. 7/1/2025; reaches Medicaid risk-based managed care via -5(a)(3)): an authorization 'shall be valid for at least one (1) year'. CareSource's July 2025 IHCP Works deck: 'Approved Authorization — Valid for 365 calendar days'. But the IHCP Behavioral Health Services module (PROMOD00039 v4.4, 7/23/2026), which covers FFS and managed care ABA, still says 'Each PA request for ABA therapy services is limited to up to six months'. Unsettled whether -26 overrides the ABA 6-month request span or only governs validity. indiana-medicaid (FFS) is out of the statute's scope and stands.

hygiene.issue: 72 section-level cite URLs across the directory do not appear in their guide's top-level `sources` array (audit run 2026-09-17, 193 guides).
hygiene.impact: Cosmetic only — PayerPage appends orphan cites to the numbered source list at render time, so readers still see every source. The `sources` array is simply not a complete bibliography.

hygiene.issue: Blocker classification for licensed proprietary criteria (MCG B-806-T, InterQual, internal UM guidelines).
hygiene.impact: Filing them as blocker 'document' creates permanent debt that no human retrieval can ever close, and implies the payer is withholding something it could publish. A new blocker value 'licensed' was added 2026-09-17 for exactly this case; the page renders it as 'Licensed criteria' / 'In licensed criteria:'.
hygiene.resolve: Reclassify existing MCG/InterQual-blocked facts from 'document' to 'licensed', and never open document requests for them.

coverageAfter.fieldPresence: all 12 structured fields at 100%; assessmentPA/treatmentPA/dxRequired at 100%
coverageAfter.note: 'document' is the only real debt — 292 facts whose answer is written down in a file we could not open, closeable through carelu.com/sources. 'per-case' (489) and 'licensed' (9) never close and must not be chased: the first is 'ask the plan', which is the finished answer, and the second sits in proprietary MCG/InterQual criteria that are never published. Enforced by `npm run payers:check`.
coverageAfter.caveat: Coverage counts fields PRESENT. Watch the verified ratio, not the presence ratio — presence can hit 100% while quality falls.
